title: An 'expensive price to pay': Friends, relatives of victim say he didn't need to die
article: The break-and-enter suspect fatally shot by a Vanderhoof RCMP officer Sunday was the father of two young children, an artist and a man relatives say paid too high a price for his alleged crime.

Kevin St. Arnaud, 29, was shot after police responded to a break- and-enter call at the Rexall Drug Store in Vanderhoof's Co-op Mall. Once on the scene, an officer at the rear of the business spotted St. Arnaud fleeing the area on foot.

He was then pursued by a police vehicle as well as on foot to the nearby field of the Nechako Valley Secondary School. During the pursuit, police say, St. Arnaud turned on the officer and approached him aggressively.
Police say the officer, who has two years of experience on the force, opened fire, shooting three times and killing St. Arnaud when he refused to listen to directions.
"It was a pretty expensive price to pay for what he was up to," uncle Guy St. Arnaud of Prince George said last night. "A little bit extreme, I guess, with the three shells."
"He was the father of two little children and they're fatherless now," said stepfather Brian Young, who lives in Vanderhoof. "It's a crime, really."

Delores Young, St. Arnaud's mother, described her son as a welder, a welding artist, painter and a soapstone carver who was abandoned by his birth father as a child and had a lot of problems with police but whose life was basically "good."
"He had some real issues, real anger," she said last night from Vanderhoof.
St. Arnaud's current girlfriend, who did not wish to be named, said her partner "was everything you'd want in a friend.
"Kevin was a man who was good to children. He had lots of love to give," she said.
Delores Young said the family is awaiting a coroner's report and the results of an internal police investigation before deciding what to do next.
"We have to deal with the grief first, I feel. He's not going anywhere. There's no saving him," she said.
A memorial service for St. Arnaud is scheduled for Dec. 28 at the United Church in Vanderhoof.
An autopsy was conducted yesterday.
The officer involved in the shooting is on regular time off and has been provided with personal and emotional support by the RCMP.
Meanwhile, as family and friends of the dead man try to piece together their lives just a few days before Christmas, police are trying to put together the events of that cold and snowy morning.
A forensic examination of the shooting scene has been completed and stolen property from the drug store and three shell casings recovered.
St. Arnaud's body remained in the field where he fell overnight Sunday and into the day Monday while the scene was being looked over. No weapons were found.
"Of course, the area was all snowy and we got another dump of snow \[shortly after\]," said
Const. Mike Caira of the North District Major Crimes Unit.

"In and around where the shooting happened was searched, but between the building and the roads any number of things could have happened. The search may still reveal something and that has to be done by the officers investigating."
